title: Derive P-CURRENT-HANDLE: no thread resumes a coroutine while it runs
why: W47-PREMISES-CORO-PLUGIN derives P-CORO-HANDLE for the loop-owner census (loop_owner_coro_plugin.rs; rule 10p's amendment): at the 90978ac6 export every typed access of struct flb_input_coro::coro, struct flb_libco_in_params::{coro,coll} and both input_coro_list members stands in the input coroutine's closed set (flb_input_coro_create, flb_input_coro_collect, input_params_set, input_pre_cb_collect, flb_input_coro_resume, flb_coro_resume, flb_input_coro_destroy, flb_coro_destroy), a handle is only dereferenced, tested, stored into a handle member or passed on within the set, the creation and hand-off are called only there, and input_coro_list is only initialised and appended to. What is left is the running coroutine's handle of itself: flb_coro_resume stores the handle as the thread's current coroutine (flb_coro_set) and flb_coro_get()/co_active() hand it to code that may publish it (connection->coroutine, flb_time_sleep's timer) for a later resume. The census needs that such a resume never happens while the coroutine runs (after its first segment began and before it yields), which it does not derive. Size: 25 flb_coro_get/co_active call sites in the program (listed in the census's typed.premises); every discharge that rests on a dropped coroutine route rests on it (11 sites at 90978ac6 configured). DISCHARGE: derive, per site, that the published handle is resumed only by the thread-local event loop of the thread that runs the coroutine (flb_engine_evl_get()/set) after the body yields, or that the body resumes nothing while it runs, measured on the census with the old test still not discharged.

title: Derive P-THREADED-SET-BEFORE-START: the remaining threaded-flag writes precede the instance's start
why: W47-PREMISES-CORO-PLUGIN derives the immutable threaded flag down to a named residual: at the 90978ac6 export every write of struct flb_input_instance::is_threaded is flb_input_set_property's in its prop_key_check("threaded", …) arm (src/flb_input.c:1002, key parameter unassigned), or into an instance its writer created itself (flb_input_new's flb_calloc at :631, trace_chunk_pipeline_thread's flb_input_new at src/flb_chunk_trace.c:189, no call before either write reaching collector_create); 31 flb_input_set_property calls pass another literal key and cannot write it. Left: the two creation writes and the 4 setter calls whose key is not one literal (src/flb_lib.c:328 flb_input_set, src/flb_config.c:1384 and :1388 configure_plugins_type, plugins/custom_calyptia/calyptia.c:264 set_fleet_input_properties) must run before the instance they write starts, since a collector is attached to the loop the flag selects when it is created. Size: 6 sites; every discharge at 90978ac6 rests on it (11 configured). DISCHARGE: derive for each site that it precedes the written instance's flb_input_instance_init on every path (or writes an instance not yet published), measured on the census.

title: Derive the plugin-directory registrations the census leaves on the coroutine route
why: W47-PREMISES-CORO-PLUGIN derives P-PLUGIN-DIR's registration half per collector registrant: a directory's descriptor flags decide a registrant only when every registration's instance is an unassigned parameter chained through direct calls to a callback stored only in that directory's descriptors (P-CALLBACK-INSTANCE derived for those fields) or to a collector callback of the directory so registered. At the 90978ac6 export 61 of 88 registrants registered only under plugins/ derive; 27 keep the coroutine route: 22 whose descriptor callback's P-CALLBACK-INSTANCE meets plugins/in_node_exporter_metrics/ne.c:157 (a cb_init dispatch of ne's own collector table that does not pass the instance whose p it goes through, reaching every cb_init registrant: in_ebpf, in_unix_socket, in_windows_exporter_metrics x17, in_winevtlog, in_winlog, in_winstat), 4 registering on a value that is not one variable (ctx->ins and the like: in_etw, in_forward, in_tcp, in_udp), 1 whose chain reaches no descriptor callback (in_podman_metrics's in_metrics_init). No site moves on them (each is not discharged or unresolved for another reason); the census reads 27 more coroutine edges (33,529 -> 33,556 configured). DISCHARGE: key the ne.c dispatch by its record, read an instance stored once into a context field from the callback's instance parameter, measured on the census.

title: Record the narrowed residual premises as held provider contracts
why: W47-PREMISES-CORO-PLUGIN narrows its three premises to P-CURRENT-HANDLE (flb_coro_get/co_active), P-THREADED-SET-BEFORE-START (flb_input_set_property's threaded arm and two creation writes) and P-DESCRIPTOR-FLAGS-BY-MEMBER (a struct flb_input_plugin's flags written only through member accesses, beside P-REGISTERED-DESCRIPTORS), stated in rule 10p and the census's typed.premises report. The observations-as-contracts rule asks such facts to be written as quirin-provider-fluent-bit contracts, pinned and held for review. This card did not add them: declaring flb_coro_get or flb_input_set_property changes the per-unit verdict at every call site in the corpus, system and tail-pause slice (a held declaration is Pending where undeclared was Unknown), an integrator decision with its arbiter measurement (as W47-LOOP-OWNER-INSTANCE-FLOW's §6). Size: 3 residual premises, 2 callee declarations (flb_coro_get, flb_input_set_property) and one descriptor clause. DISCHARGE: the declarations exist in fluent_bit/, held with the observation as their reason, pinned at 66910c10, 046accf6 and the 90978ac6 export, with the corpus/system/slice movement attributed.
